Honestly, it's fun keeping up on this, because I have no idea how things will turn out.  On one hand, trends are definitely pointing to people accepting all-digital consoles.  Even if Sony isn't as reliable as Steam, the fact that there is already a successful digital console at all means that the transition could work.

But on the other hand, when Sony needed to approach this crossroads carefully, instead they just arrogantly antagonized the player base, and they'll be remembered for that.  Even once the scandal isn't the new fresh thing anymore, this is how people see Sony now.

And then there's the untenable price of the PS6.  And the fact that hard drive space is expensive.  And the fact that internet is inconsistent for a lot of people doomed Stadia, and now Sony wants to rely on it.  Sure there will still be demand for a PS6 (if there still is one) but if the logistics of the console don't add up, then the sales will drop.  These products CAN fail.  So who knows?
